summary: This section explains how official documents can be sent to a company, its officers, the Registrar, or its members. Documents can generally be delivered by post, courier, leaving them at the office, or through approved electronic methods. Members also have the right to ask for a specific delivery mode if they pay the fees decided by the company.
points: Documents can be sent to a company or its officer at the registered office by registered post, speed post, courier, hand delivery, or prescribed electronic modes.
A depository may send beneficial ownership records to the company using electronic or other modes.
Documents can be sent to the Registrar or a member by post, registered post, speed post, courier, hand delivery at their address, or prescribed electronic modes.
A member can request a specific mode of delivery for documents.
Members must pay the fees determined by the company in its annual general meeting for their requested delivery mode.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited needed to send important notices to its members and shareholders. Rahul, a member of Meera Textiles Private Limited, preferred to receive all his documents through a specific postal mode rather than electronic methods. Rahul formally requested this particular mode from the company. To cover the arrangement, Rahul agreed to pay the fees that had been decided by the company during its annual general meeting. Meanwhile, the company sent its official records to its registered office using a courier service that provided proof of delivery, ensuring they followed the proper legal steps for service of documents.

terms.meaning: The official main address of a company where all communications and notices are sent.
An organization that holds securities in electronic form on behalf of investors.
The government authority responsible for the registration and regulation of companies.

watch: Remember that a member can choose a specific delivery mode only by paying the fee decided at the annual general meeting.
